📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, BYD just got some good news in its Defender-copycat court battle with JLR. After JLR had BYD’s Netherlands offices raided and documents seized, a Dutch court has now handed BYD an early win, ordering JLR to destroy the documents or face a penalty.

After BYD opened orders for the Ti 7 in Europe and the UK in late July, many (including us at Electrek) compared it to the iconic Land Rover Defender, with its boxy, rugged (yet still elegant) SUV design.

BYD even described it as having “an unapologetically boxy profile” that delivers “the imposing, chunky design that finds favour among SUV buyers, yet delivers a contemporary look.”.

In August, authorities on behalf of the British luxury automaker raided BYD’s offices in the Netherlands without prior warning and seized digital records.

On November 11, a Dutch court in The Hague ruled against JLR and ordered the firm to destroy the seized documents, which included launch aims and other technical data, so they wouldn’t fall into anyone else’s hands.

JLR must destroy the documents within 24 hours of the ruling or face a fine of €50,000 ($55,000) for every hour it is delayed, with a maximum penalty of up to €500,000 ($553,000).

According to recent reports, within 24 hours of destroying it, JLR must also provide BYD with third-party confirmation that it has been destroyed. The court also rejected the British automaker’s request to pay a €500,000 ($553,000) fine.

According to Autoweek Netherlands, the ruling is based on the fact that JLR doesn’t need the documents, noting that the Ti 7 has not yet been sold in the European Union.

BYD won the ruling, and JLR is prohibited from taking any further legal action under the initial seizure order, but JLR has already begun summary proceedings over the infringement in Rotterdam and The Hague.

JLR claims that the Ti 7 SUV is a “slavish imitation” and infringes on the intellectual property of the Land Rover Defender and that BYD stripped down the Defender to reverse-engineer some of its technology.

Recent findings suggest that before the raid, BYD claims it fully cooperated with JLR’s requests. BYD’s lawyers called the British automakers’ raid a “fishing expedition” and claimed that “too many files were seized.”.

According to recent reports, the Ti 7 is on sale starting at £47,995 ($64,000) in the UK, on the road. That’s over £20,000 ($26,500) less than the plug-in Defender 110, which starts at £71,840 ($95,500) in the UK.

It has a seven-seat arrangement, which BYD stated was specifically designed for the European and UK markets.

As the first vehicle in the UK based on its DM-p (Dual Mode performance) powertrain, BYD said the Ti 7 “vastly exceeds the closest competition,” seemingly another jab at the Defender.

"JLR believes BYD stripped down the Defender to reverse engineer some of its technology".

Sources indicate that reverse engineering isn't illegal. Patent infringement is illegal.

Competition strip down each other's product all the time. As long as they don't use the "exact" same technology, it isn't a copy right issue.

The setup uses three electric motors and a 1.5-liter turbocharged engine, delivering a combined 402 hp (408 PS), enabling it to accelerate from 0 to 62 mph in 4.8 seconds.

Recent findings suggest that the engine primarily powers a 35.6 kWh BYD Blade Battery, which provides a pure-electric WLTP driving range of up to 74 miles. In the city, it has an electric range of up to 102 miles.

Available exclusively in the UK in the flagship Excellence AWD trim, BYD claims that the Ti 7 offers “a level of equipment that exceeds anything that its rivals can offer at this price point.”.

Sources indicate that we should learn more about the BYD and JLR legal battle soon. Check back for updates, as this story is still ongoing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fidelity Investments now supports three newly introduced cryptocurrencies on its retail crypto trading platform: Chainlink (LINK), Aave (AAVE) and Uniswap (UNI).

Industry observers note that the firm expanded from five available cryptocurrencies to eight on Nov. 24. In just one day, Fidelity added the same number of digital assets that it had added in the four years since it first made Bitcoin and Ether available for customer trading.

Eligible U.S. customers can trade these three tokens on the Fidelity website and app. Some states may have limited access to Fidelity's services.

In a recent development, fidelity's three new listings include tokens that represent different areas of decentralized finance. Aave is a lending protocol where people can deposit crypto assets to earn interest or use them as collateral for loans. AAVE token holders can vote on changes to the protocol's lending markets and other aspects of its operation.

Uniswap is a decentralized trading platform where people can trade different tokens using shared pools of assets provided by other users. UNI is the Uniswap governance token.

Chainlink provides the data that blockchain apps need to operate. For example, a lending protocol might use a Chainlink price feed to assess the value of collateral for a borrower's loan. Chainlink (LINK) tokens are used to pay for services provided on its network.

Recent findings suggest that fidelity Crypto started accepting customers from its waitlist in November 2022. At the time, the only two cryptocurrencies it offered were Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH). By March 2023, Fidelity was offering its service to more eligible U.S. investors, but these were still the only cryptocurrencies it allowed customers to trade.

Industry observers note that on July 17, 2024, Fidelity added Litecoin (LTC) to its list of cryptocurrencies, bringing the total to three. Over a year later, on Oct. 23, 2025, the company introduced Solana (SOL). In addition to individual retail accounts, Solana became available for crypto IRAs, wealth managers and institutional clients.

Fidelity added its fifth cryptocurrency on Feb. 4, 2026, when it released Fidelity Digital Dollar (FIDD) as its first stablecoin available to retail and institutional investors. Eligible consumers can exchange or redeem each FIDD token for $1. Fidelity waives its usual crypto trading fee when users exchange FIDD for dollars.

Industry observers note that the U.S. Department of Justice filed a civil forfeiture action on Nov. 23 seeking to recover more than $1.1 billion in USDC allegedly stolen from Binance by North Korean hackers.

The assets had previously been frozen under a restraining order obtained by the government. The latest filing represents another step toward recovering funds following the Oct. 29 attack, which reportedly resulted in more than $6 billion in stolen cryptocurrency.

The DOJ claimed that its recent civil forfeiture action focuses on over $1.1 billion worth of USD Coin (USDC), a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar and issued by Circle.

According to recent reports, U.S. authorities noted they had helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion in cryptocurrency since the theft. The case highlights the role of cooperation between law enforcement agencies and crypto companies in tracking and recovering stolen digital assets.

Strategy purchased another 457 BTC for approximately $29.6 million, according to a Nov. 23 report based on the firm's SEC filing.

According to recent reports, the latest acquisition was made at an average price of $64,898 per Bitcoin, bringing Strategy's holdings to approximately 851,305 BTC. The organization has spent around $64.23 billion accumulating Bitcoin at an average purchase price of $75,446.

The firm's recent purchase comes as the leading cryptocurrency has been struggling to rebound from the heavy sell-off that recently dragged it to a two-plus-year low.

In a recent development, XRP briefly climbed above $1 on Monday after Nvidia's Jensen Huang returned to his roles as CEO and president, triggering a sharp rally in U.S. technology stocks and broader risk assets.

On Binance's XRP/USDT perpetual contract, the token moved from approximately $0.94 to $1.02 within minutes after 14:00 UTC, before retreating to around $0.984.

CoinGlass data cited by U.Today highlighted that XRP short liquidations exceeded long liquidations by 578%.

Across the crypto market, 110,663 traders were liquidated for $660.89 million over the past 24 hours, while shorts accounted for $515.94 million of that amount.

sonnen’s new smart breakers help your home battery last longer

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (753 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A home battery can do more during a blackout if it isn’t busy running nonessential, energy-hungry appliances.
  • It has been revealed that the companies announced today that they’re integrating ADAPT Energy’s controls and Eaton AbleEdge smart breakers into the SOLRITE–sonnen virtual power plant (VPP).
  • The announcement doesn’t specify pricing, how many homes will receive it, or when existing customers can get it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A home battery can do more during a blackout if it isn’t busy running nonessential, energy-hungry appliances. sonnen and SOLRITE Energy are putting that same principle to work for the grid, adding smart breakers that can temporarily switch off selected household loads while batteries help meet electricity demand.

It has been revealed that the companies announced today that they’re integrating ADAPT Energy’s controls and Eaton AbleEdge smart breakers into the SOLRITE–sonnen virtual power plant (VPP). The setup combines sonnenHub with breakers that manage power-hungry equipment, both during outages and when the grid needs help.

The announcement doesn’t specify pricing, how many homes will receive it, or when existing customers can get it.

Industry observers note that A VPP connects home batteries into a network so they can work together as a larger energy resource. This addition gives SOLRITE another way to respond: in addition to controlling the batteries, it can reduce the amount of electricity that participating homes use.

Sources indicate that sonnen and SOLRITE used the example of a pool pump, as it’s energy-intensive, nonessential, and runs for longer periods. When an event begins, ADAPT temporarily switches off the pool pump while the sonnen battery sends electricity to the grid.

Sources indicate that with less battery power going toward the pump, more can flow to the grid. Across participating homes, that gives the VPP more flexibility than relying on battery dispatch alone.

Industry observers note that homeowners have to opt in to that grid participation, and ADAPT will switch off only pre-approved household loads. Joining the VPP program doesn’t give the operator blanket permission to turn off anything in the house.

“Instead of putting the pressure on homeowners to change the way their home is wired, and to manually manipulate loads during an outage, we’re putting intelligence into their energy system, which provides a seamless and automatic backup power experience for their home,” remarked Troy Morgan, president of PanTech Design, the developer of ADAPT Energy.

The breakers also tackle a practical problem with home backup: Big appliances can drain a battery quickly, and the surge of power some equipment needs to start can overload a backup system just as an outage begins.

In a recent development, ADAPT coordinates the smart breakers with the sonnen battery to automatically switch off large loads during backup operation. When grid power returns, it restores them, so homeowners don’t have to go around resetting individual circuits.

That also gives homeowners more flexibility later. According to the companies, changing which smart-breaker-controlled loads are switched off during an outage doesn’t require rewiring those circuits.

It has been revealed that the installation benefit matters, too. Some backup setups require electricians to move selected circuits into a separate panel. This system manages compatible circuits where their breakers already sit, which the companies say reduces installation complexity and inspection work.

It has been revealed that whole-home backup still has limits. Automatically managing large loads helps the available battery capacity go further; it doesn’t mean every appliance can run at once throughout an outage.

In a recent development, SOLRITE finances, builds, and owns residential solar-plus-storage projects through what it calls Virtual Power Plant Agreements, with no upfront cost to homeowners. It says it operates in Texas, California, Connecticut, Massachusetts, and Illinois, with more markets planned.

Review: Engwe’s M20 3.0 is a 60V Super73 killer at a fraction of the price

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (956 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Engwe has impressed us repeatedly with its value e-bikes at lower-than-believable prices.
  • The Engwe M20 3.0 is a specs monster and blows away the original version of the bike released in 2023:.
  • Industry observers note that the M20 is fairly easy to assemble.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Engwe has impressed us repeatedly with its value e-bikes at lower-than-believable prices. But lately, the brand is climbing the value chain with impressive e-bikes that aren’t just great value but also pack strong specs and impressive features. The Engwe M20 3.0 is a great example….

The Engwe M20 3.0 is a specs monster and blows away the original version of the bike released in 2023:.

Industry observers note that the M20 is fairly easy to assemble. At just over 100lbs, it is a bit hard to move around, but once assembled, it feels like a pretty impressive piece of machinery. I love the street tires on here instead of pretending to be an off-roader. Dual bright headlights and brake light with turn signals really give this thing some street cred. Adding to the safety roster, Engwe upgraded the quad-piston brakes with sporty red calipers and 202 mm rotors. This is not a value bike. The rear suspension is tight, which is great for 2 riders but might feel stiff out of the box for light riders. The seat is *chef’s kiss* even for 2 riders. Very soft and comfortable but not too soft. It even has a little ‘gas tank’ storage area aft the seat, which is keyed and enough to hold a few sandwiches, some riding gloves, or a small purse.

One gripe: There are 3 sets of keys on here, the aforementioned storage area and one set each for each battery. We’d love to see these things keyed together.

Industry observers note that the bike/moped/moto came with a huge 1.2 kW battery (or 2 in our case – unless you have a 80-mile commute, 1 should be plenty) that must be charged individually. But with a 60V 8A charger, each one only takes about 2-3 hours to charge, which is impressive.

In a recent development, I did not expect to like the ride of this thing as much as I did. We can dispense with the pleasantries here; it came set to Class 2 mode with a 20mph top speed and stickers to match; a quick Google search will show you how to open this up to 40mph open mode. I take responsibility for my own actions.

According to recent reports, the first thing you’ll notice here is that the motor is whisper-quiet, and with the street tires, there is very little road noise, even at 35mph. The half throttle is plenty responsive, a lot more so than the cadence sensor on the pedals, which are vestigial at best here. Those substantial brakes are a bit softer than I’d prefer, but given a good squeeze, those 203mm rotors and quad-piston hydraulic brakes are going to stop you, the 100lb bike, and your passenger/cargo fairly quickly.

My girlfriend and I got pulled over for the first time in my e-biking life as I was picking her up at the coffee shop. The cop was immediately apologetic because “he thought we were kids” and not the 50-year-olds under the helmets he encountered. Then he noticed the pedals and stated that we’re all clear and that what we were on looked like a motorcycle and that a couple of e-moto kids had gotten into accidents recently, one hit by a drunk driver and who is still in a coma. While he was already letting us go, I pointed out the Class 2 sticker on the bike, and he gave me the thumbs-up as we sped off at 30mph. This M20 passed the local police test with flying colors. I can’t guarantee you’ll have the same experience in your jurisdiction.

Industry observers note that most of my gripes on this e-bike are inherent to the form factor. It is heavy at over 100 lbs, but you’d expect that with a 3.3kW motor, 2.4kW of batteries, and room for two. That mentioned, don’t buy this bike if you need to take it up stairs or initiative to pedal it without assist. In fact, this isn’t a bikepath bike or a put it on the back of your car bike. And, don’t buy this bike if you like to pedal. It’s too massive and fast. This is a 35 mph roads bike. Also 3 sets of keys?

I did not expect to love this bike as much as I have. It is the perfect train station bike for me, and as a bonus, it is a great way to take my girlfriend to the coffee shop on the weekends. It has fat tires, great suspension, a cushy seat, and strong, smooth acceleration and confidence-inspiring braking. It looks cool enough for the cops to think I’m a kid picking up his girlfriend, and it has so much range that I probably won’t need to charge it monthly. At $1399-$1699 (10% off) depending on battery config, this is less than half the price of some of the pricier and admittedly more stylish Super73 options out there.

It has been revealed that I understand that some will fault Engwe for selling a 3.3kW motor e-bike as a class 2 e-bike. But I genuinely feel safer on the road, being able to go at the 35mph speed that cars are going rather than forcing them to go around me. Plus, it isn’t like every single car on the road goes over the speed limit. So why not bikes too?

The Engwe M20 3.0 is over the limit but in all of the best possible ways.

Industry News: End of Crypto Trading? How AI Replaces Ones Who Pumped Bitcoin (BTC)

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (749 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: U

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the “pump” trade could be taken to new extremes.
  • All things considered, agents may exacerbate many of the existing problems with crypto, from short lived moves/reversals, to dangerous herding and even more pronounced drawdowns.
  • Automation is not necessarily a fresh occurrence in the space, from simple rule-based trading (implement a certain set of rules when X occurs) to algo trading (use algos to spread out trading activity to avoid market impact), but it appears to be shifting from humans implementing strategies to letting AI make decisions and execute.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the “pump” trade could be taken to new extremes. While some may still be able to use their influence to promote a token, causing others to pile in, it could now be left up to AI to scour socials/wallet activity for abnormal trading volume, assess momentum rankings, etc. and execute on these opportunities faster than those that may be slower to react.

All things considered, agents may exacerbate many of the existing problems with crypto, from short lived moves/reversals, to dangerous herding and even more pronounced drawdowns.

Automation is not necessarily a fresh occurrence in the space, from simple rule-based trading (implement a certain set of rules when X occurs) to algo trading (use algos to spread out trading activity to avoid market impact), but it appears to be shifting from humans implementing strategies to letting AI make decisions and execute.

A February 2026 study from the Journal of Futures Markets found sub-second trading patterns in BTC/ETH perpetual/spot markets exhibiting behavior consistent with algo trading for liquidity, increasing volatility and trading costs with no significant impact on prices.

In August 2026, Binance rolled out Agent OS allowing builders to access exchange trading functionality and data via AI agents.

According to recent reports, coinbase Ventures released a comprehensive breakdown of the crypto agentic stack from data, to agent building tools, to execution/compliance in November. Instead of dictating each trade, people may be able to assign high-level goals (i.e. follow momentum, hedge position, etc.) for agents to implement 24/7.

Sources indicate that automation will likely accelerate across the crypto space. While macro events, ETF inflows/outflows, large holders, etc. will still have an impact on Bitcoin, it’s likely that many more aspects/trades will become automated.

Time will tell how pervasive agentic trading will become, but the era of a small group of traders/influencers/chat rooms able to move the needle via FOMO/hype seems poised to face stiff competition from AI that never sleeps.

AI is not necessarily intelligent. A 2026 study published in the journal Frontiers in Blockchain studied machine-learning strategies using crypto market data and found that many strategies became highly overfit and offered no viable edge for retail traders once realistic trading fees were taken into account.

Industry observers note that also, strategies that performed well on one cryptocurrency did not necessarily perform well on others. Faster processing speeds can’t make bad data good, can’t identify all false narratives and can’t insulate a strategy from sudden shifts in market regimes.

Are institutional investors still relevant? Can they protect themselves? Absolutely.

Institutions are (and will continue to be) an vital source of capital, liquidity and price discovery (particularly for Bitcoin). A 2026 study using BTC data from 2012–2025 found that as the market has matured, Bitcoin has seen increased trading volume, decreasing transaction costs and increasing market efficiency.

According to recent reports, wintermute reported that in the first half of 2026 institutional clients accounted for 72% of total spot trading volume on its OTC desk (note: this is Wintermute’s OTC desk and is not representative of the entire market). It’s also worth noting that many institutional investors do employ quantitative strategies and state-of-the-art execution technologies.

While larger investors may have access to better data, faster infrastructure, cross-venue surveillance capabilities and stricter risk management protocols (and can limit their exposure and monitor abnormal order flow), there’s only so much that institutional investors can do to protect themselves.

According to recent reports, institutional investors can’t control a 24/7 global market with liquidity spread across multiple venues and derivatives markets. They also can’t assume that all AIs are created equal/safe (as Binance’s launch of its own AI demonstrated prompt injection risks and limited visibility into external AIs’ trading logic/reasons for trading).

Finally, during times of stress, risk management/contingency protocols (used by many investors) could be a crowded exit for funds that employ similar strategies.

According to recent reports, the future is not “AI replaces every trader.” It will likely see continued automation of certain aspects of trading (i.e. execution, short-term alpha hunting, etc.) and a continued shift in the value-add that humans bring to the table (i.e. capital allocation, risk management, original research, granting/trading bots permission to trade, etc.).

While AI/bots may continue to squeeze spreads in normal market conditions, they may exacerbate drawdowns/cascades during times of market stress as strategies compete with one another.

At the end of the day, Bitcoin will still be bought/sold, it’s just a question of who gets to make those decisions.

In a recent development, are Ripple’s XRP, Cardano (ADA), and Polygon (POL) losing their appeal among crypto investors in 2026? Ben Simpson, founder of crypto investment platform Collective Shift, has named all three among six altcoins he indicates he wouldn’t touch with a 10-foot pole, citing concerns ranging from weak network activity and questionable valuations to intensifying competition. His blunt assessment raises fresh questions about which altcoins have the strongest fundamentals to survive the increasingly competitive crypto market.

In his post on X, Simpson acknowledged XRP’s role in enabling near-instant, inexpensive payments on the XRP Ledger but argued that the token lacks a compelling mechanism for capturing the value generated by Ripple’s business growth.

According to recent reports, XRP enables fast, low-cost payments on the XRP Ledger.My issue with XRP is it's "value capture".When a business grows, I want to see how that success benefits the token I'm holding. In this case, there is none. Ripple can grow its revenue, but holders don't receive those….

In a recent development, his main concern is that Ripple’s commercial success does not necessarily translate into direct financial benefits for XRP holders. Even as the San Francisco-headquartered organization expands its revenue and boosts its payment operations, investors do not receive a share of those profits.

He also pointed out that Ripple does not use its business earnings to buy back XRP, a mechanism that could potentially create additional demand for the token. For Simpson, the absence of both profit-sharing and a buyback program makes it difficult to establish a direct link between Ripple’s growing business and XRP’s price in the long term.

He considers these shortcomings significant enough to keep XRP off his investment list, despite the network’s payment capabilities.

In a recent development, simpson also expressed reservations about Cardano, arguing that its adoption level does not justify its market valuation. Although ADA powers a blockchain designed to support smart contracts and decentralized applications, he believes the network is generating relatively little economic activity compared with its overall market size.

To support his argument, Simpson pointed to Cardano’s fee generation, claiming that the network collected just $140,000 in transaction fees over a 30-day period despite ADA carrying a market capitalization of approximately $7.5 billion.

In a recent development, for him, the disparity raises questions about whether Cardano is attracting enough customers and developers to sustain its valuation. He believes a blockchain with such a substantial market capitalization should demonstrate considerably stronger usage and demand for its services.

Recent findings suggest that ultimately, Simpson’s concern is that Cardano needs to translate its technological ambitions and established ecosystem into greater real-world activity. Without a meaningful increase in network usage, he appears unconvinced that ADA offers an attractive investment proposition.

Sources indicate that polygon also made the list, with concerns centered on the growing competition in Ethereum’s scaling ecosystem. Although POL supports a network designed to make transactions faster and cheaper, the increasing number of competing blockchain solutions has made it harder for Polygon to maintain a distinctive advantage.

Simpson’s concern is that newer networks are offering similar benefits, including lower transaction costs and faster processing speeds, leaving Polygon with fewer obvious ways to differentiate itself.

With several projects competing for developers, users, and blockchain activity, POL faces the challenge of proving why it deserves a place ahead of its rivals.

Beyond XRP, Cardano, and Polygon, three other cryptocurrencies also fell short of Ben Simpson’s investment criteria: Sui (SUI), Ronin (RON), and Dogwifhat (WIF). Unlike his concerns about the first three crypto projects, his reservations about these tokens stem largely from changing investment convictions, disappointing adoption, and excessive reliance on market hype.

It has been revealed that sui was among the projects Simpson previously held before changing his investment outlook. The high-speed blockchain is designed to support decentralized applications and transactions, but he eventually dumped his SUI holdings at a loss of between 20% and 30% after his investment thesis changed. He did not elaborate on the specific developments that prompted his decision.

Industry observers note that ronin was another project he abandoned after its growth failed to match his expectations. Initially attracted by the potential of blockchain gaming, the pundit bought into the network, which uses RON for transaction fees and staking. However, the anticipated expansion in gaming adoption did not materialize as he had hoped, prompting him to exit the position relatively promptly. He argued that strong sector potential means little without meaningful retail participation.

WIF, meanwhile, represented a different kind of investment mistake. Simpson admitted that his decision to buy the Solana-based meme coin was driven largely by hype rather than underlying fundamentals. After his investment thesis changed, he sold his holdings to limit further losses.

His experience with WIF appears to have reinforced his preference for cryptocurrencies backed by stronger fundamentals rather than speculative excitement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Bitwise XRP ETF traded an average of about $14 million a day over its first year on the market, resulting in over $3.5 billion in total trading volume, according to Bitwise.

In a post on X commemorating the Bitwise XRP ETF's first anniversary, Bitwise said the fund had recorded over $667 million in net inflows and had more than $376 million in assets under management (AUM) since launch.

Bitwise's XRP ETF started trading on Nov. 20, 2025, on NYSE Arca. It trades under the same ticker as the cryptocurrency it holds, XRP.

Investors can use the ETF's shares to track the price of the token through their brokerage accounts. The fund holds the XRP on behalf of investors. At launch, the ETF charged a 0.34% annual management fee. It also offered a fee waiver for the first $500 million in assets for the first month.

According to recent reports, the $3.5 billion in trading volume is the total value of purchases and sales of the ETF's shares. This means the same ETF shares could trade repeatedly. If an investor sells their shares to another investor, that transaction increases trading volume. But the total XRP held in the fund doesn't change in that case.

On the other hand, the $667 million in net inflows represents the total dollar value of upcoming shares issued over the past year minus redeemed shares.

It has been revealed that AUM represents the total dollar value of a fund's assets at a specific moment. Since the fund's total assets are valued in dollars, AUM can fall below cumulative net inflows if the price of XRP declines, even as investors continue to put money into the fund.

Industry observers note that the quarterly report filed by Bitwise with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) highlights the impact of investor demand and XRP's price on the fund over the past year.

The net asset value of the fund increased from $299.1 million at the end of June to $614.9 million at the end of September.

Over $315.7 million was added to the fund's net assets during that quarter. Just over half of that $315.7 million came from upcoming share creations.

In a recent development, the fund issued latest shares with a total dollar value of $210.7 million. It also redeemed $32.8 million in shares during that quarter. So that left about $178 million in net new creations.

The fund issued 13.75 million shares and redeemed 2.42 million shares.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The U.S Department of Justice (DOJ) has taken legal action to recover more than $1.1 billion in cryptos stolen from Binance on 29th October 2026. With this move, the government has now moved beyond simply freezing the stolen funds and is now seeking their legal forfeiture.

According to the DOJ, the stolen funds had already been placed under a restraining order, which was the reason why they were prevented from being transferred or accessed while authorities pursued recovery efforts.

Remarking on the same, Attorney General for National Security M. Scott Proctor remarked,.

The Department of Justice has long prioritized victims and their rights, and the commencement of this forfeiture action so soon after the restraint of these same assets reflects our commitment to ensuring that victims remain at the forefront of our work.

Binance suffered a cryptocurrency theft worth more than $6.3 billion, which the U.S authorities linked to North Korean cyber hackers.

Following the attack, the hackers allegedly used sophisticated laundering techniques to move the stolen cryptocurrency across different wallets and potentially convert it.

However, the FBI, U.S Secret Service, and the IRS has worked alongside private-sector companies to track the transactions and identify wallets holding the stolen funds.

As its stands, the U.S. government has frozen and seized nearly $3 billion worth of cryptocurrencies from multiple sources since the Binance theft. The latest $1.1 billion forfeiture action is part of this broader recovery effort and does not represent an additional $1.1 billion on top of the nearly $3 billion already recovered or restrained.

If this forfeiture is successful, the action could help return the recovered assets to their rightful owners.

XRP reportedly traded at just 29 cents in Kraken’s Canadian-dollar market during a sharp, localized sell-off discussed by crypto commentator Crypto Sensei.

His video examines whether the trades reflected an exchange-specific liquidity problem rather than a broader XRP collapse, alongside falling ledger activity and disputed price forecasts.

Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong remarked on X that the organization is repurchasing stock in the fourth quarter because investors are overlooking the potential of the payments business for AI agents.

"Good to take advantage of market dislocations," said Armstrong.

Sources indicate that the organization is buying back stock using funds previously authorized for repurchases. He didn't specify the number of COIN shares, the price or the amount spent.

At the start of the quarter, Coinbase had $1.96 billion left to repurchase stock. Over the prior three months, it repurchased 37,995 shares for a total cost of $5.3 million, at an average price of $139.91. All repurchases occurred in August, according to its third-quarter report.

Recent findings suggest that coinbase's board of directors initially authorized stock buybacks of up to $1 billion in October 2024. A year later, the buyback authorization was doubled. The firm also received an option to repurchase some outstanding debt.

The board increased the buyback limit again in January 2026, bringing the total authorization to $4 billion.

It has been revealed that some buybacks have been carried out to cancel stock issued as employee compensation. By the end of September, the tech giant had repurchased 10.2 million Class A shares and canceled more than 85% of the stock issued for employee compensation since the fourth quarter of 2024. This is according to an earnings presentation.

Armstrong envisions a scenario where crypto and AI are involved in different aspects of the same transaction.

In a recent development, for example, AI agents might help owners make financial decisions and follow their instructions. Then, a crypto network may be used to transfer funds.

Coinbase wants to provide accounts, payment services, and marketplaces for humans and AI agents to use.

Recent findings suggest that "With AI, everybody has a private banker in your pocket that can help you make better financial decisions," Armstrong posted on Nov. 25.

Coinbase added its wallet and payment services to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments. This offers a way for developers to build agents on Amazon and allow the software to discover paid services. Agents can make small payments when necessary.

Now Armstrong is inviting developers to add their specialized AI models to Agentic.Market.

According to Armstrong, an AI agent can choose which specialist to hire for a task based on its capabilities and price. Coinbase provides the platform where agents can find specialists and pay them.

USDT’s market cap may now be a key metric to watch for signs of a market bottom.

Sources indicate that technically, Tether’s USDT is experiencing its most severe quarterly de-pegging since Q2 2022, which saw over 18% of its market cap drained away, totalling roughly $15 billion. Although presently the de-pegging figure is lower (around -5% so far in Q4), the consequence remains impactful. Since 2022, USDT’s market cap has increased to almost $180 billion from approximately $80 billion. This means even a smaller percentage drop now represents a much larger amount of liquidity leaving the market.

According to recent reports, the chart below highlights this trend. According to CryptoQuant data, USDT’s market cap has fallen by $8.83 billion over the 60 days leading up to the 22nd of November. Furthermore, its 30-day Moving Average is also falling, which indicates the decline is still in motion.

To put this into perspective, back in 2022 a 5% fall in Tether’s [USDT] $80 billion market cap would have caused approximately $4 billion worth of liquidity to exit the market. However, when applying the same 5% market cap reduction to today’s $180 billion figure, almost $9 billion is now leaving the market. That’s more than 2x the amount of liquidity being pulled out for the same percentage decline.

In this context, USDT’s growing market cap means its contraction now has a much bigger impact on liquidity.

Tether’s ongoing contraction further adds to the liquidity concerns.

In a recent development, TVL on DeFi platforms has decreased to just over $70 billion. This is from an approximate figure of $140 billion prior to the October 2025 crash. Thus, in just over a year, the TVL on DeFi platforms has almost been cut in half. Coupled with the reduction in USDT’s market cap, this suggests there is poor liquidity and reduced capital involvement within the crypto space.

According to recent reports, however, the impact goes beyond DeFi liquidity. As the chart below highlights, the broader crypto market has also experienced a significant bear run. So far in Q4, the market has lost over 28% of its value, reducing the market cap from $2.84 trillion down to below $1.8 trillion, meaning almost $500 billion has been erased. The key takeaway? This is the worst quarterly fall for the crypto market since Q2 2022, which also witnessed the largest-ever de-pegging of Tether’s USDT stablecoin.

According to AMBCrypto, this overlap is not random.

Rather, with Tether’s market cap now much larger than it was in 2022, even a small drop in USDT supply is now having a bigger impact on overall market liquidity. This makes USDT supply an important metric to watch during the current downturn.

Until USDT’s market cap bottoms, a sustained crypto market bottom may remain out of reach.

DeFi TVL has nearly halved to $70 billion, while the broader crypto market is down over 28% in Q4.

USDT’s shrinking market cap points to continued liquidity outflows, making its recovery a key signal to watch for a market bottom.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 U ↗ Open Full Page

XRP Ledger Bug That Makes Trading Orders Disappear Is Addressed

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (446 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: U

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today.
  • Official XRP Ledger's repository account received a proposed fix to keep only transaction-independent offer removals after a tec that should address the disappearance of failed transactions.
  • This particular change addresses a bug with order-book behavior around “tec” failures, which are failures where the transaction processing is rolled back.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Official XRP Ledger's repository account received a proposed fix to keep only transaction-independent offer removals after a tec that should address the disappearance of failed transactions.

This particular change addresses a bug with order-book behavior around “tec” failures, which are failures where the transaction processing is rolled back. In some circumstances, offers can be removed when a "tec" failure occurs, even though the transaction that triggered it never succeeded.

In one scenario, a trader could have an existing offer removed before they’re able to add a replacement (for instance, if they don’t have enough reserve to add a newly introduced offer). In another, a more complicated Flow could temporarily leave an offer unfunded, only to have funds restored if a subsequent step fails, again resulting in an offer being removed even though the transaction that triggered it failed.

To address this problem, rippled will attempt to remove offers that were marked for removal upon tec failure any time a tec failure occurs. Previously, this was attempted for certain tec error codes but not others, with some additional restrictions around Flow-related offer removals (an offer will only be marked for removal if the owner’s balance has not changed in any relevant ways during the course of the Flow).

Offers that have already expired can still be removed, but offers owned by the transactor will be skipped. This is a best effort to make sure offers are consistently added/removed from the order book and should reduce confusing trade results.

Offers to/from regular XRP accounts and balances, XRP sends are unaffected and there are no proposed API changes.

This does not change XRP supply, fees, transaction capacity, etc. and is unlikely to have any effect on XRPL usage or XRP price (other than maybe making XRPL trading more appealing to traders).

This change would mostly affect traders using decentralized exchanges (DEXs) and particularly those using complex/routed/fill-or-kill orders/self-crosses.

On November 23, XRP briefly hit $1.026 before dropping below $1. Reports indicate crypto selling in general and ETF outflows have been putting pressure on XRP lately. By November 25, XRP was trading at ~$0.92. This software change would not be a catalyst for a price recovery of XRP.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Zonveer ZX3 is one of the best values I’ve seen in electric off-road riding, and one of the most fun things I’ve ridden to date – value for the dollar. Its Black Friday sale brings the 2,800W electric dirt bike down to $1,299, $500 off its $1,799 list price.

Industry observers note that for that money, you get a 1,200Wh battery, dual hydraulic disc brakes, and full suspension in a 130 lb package. That’s a great entry point for beginners.

Recent findings suggest that zonveer is a young brand. It launched in the US in March with two bikes, the kid-sized DX1 and the ZX3, and it’s run by United Mobility, which lists its address in Dover, Delaware. It sells direct and ships from US warehouses, and Zonveer also sells the ZX3 across Europe under its own brand through its EU store.

Here’s what the ZX3 brings, according to Zonveer’s product page:.

Recent findings suggest that A hub motor means there’s no motor chain to maintain, and the NFC card and PIN unlock mean there’s no app to fight with. I like that.

In a recent development, zonveer sent me a ZX3 to test, and I’m impressed with what they shipped, knowing the cost. It isn’t trying to be a race bike. And it doesn’t need to be. Here’s my first ride review:.

Industry observers note that with 2,800W peak, it’s somewhat modest by e-moto standards. That’s exactly what makes it approachable for someone who has never ridden a dirt bike: the power is enough to have a blast on trails without being intimidating.

My girlfriend had never ridden a dirt bike before, and she got comfortable within a few minutes, and she was hooked as soon as she got the hang of it.

Industry observers note that and while testing with my girlfriend, it was clear this bike makes the most sense for lighter riders. Zonveer claims it climbs slopes of up to 30 degrees, which is optimistic for anyone over ~175 lbs, like myself. It still climbed some of the worst slopes on my land, but it did so with some difficulty, which wasn’t the case for some of my lighter friends who also rode it.

Range is the other claim to take with a grain of salt. Riding 45 miles on 1,200Wh means using under 27Wh per mile, which is e-bike efficiency on a 130 lb dirt bike with knobby tires. It’s still a lot of energy, and you can ride this long distances at lower speeds. Just expect less if you ride it hard, and that’s where the fun is at.

Zonveer’s Black Friday sale has the ZX3 at $1,299, and the company gave Electrek readers the code ELECTREK for an extra 5% off, which brings it down to $1,234.05.

The sale also includes a free water bottle and lock, and can be combined for a two-pack of ZX3s for $2,599. Shipping is free, the warranty is one year, Zonveer told us it accepts returns within 30 days on bikes ridden less than 10 miles, with a $200 restocking fee. Here’s the full refund policy.

Recent findings suggest that we’ve ridden a lot of electric two-wheelers, and the ZX3 is one of the most fun per dollar. At $1,299, or about $1,234 with our code, it’s hard to find another 1,200Wh electric dirt bike with dual hydraulic disc brakes and full suspension from a brand that ships from US warehouses.

Industry observers note that it’s not fast by e-moto standards, and the range and climbing claims are optimistic. But for beginners, and especially lighter riders, the power lands right in that sweet spot of manageable fun.   • The weekly chart above indicates a large symmetrical triangle that has formed over several market cycles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ethereum bulls face a frightening downside scenario after legendary trader and classical chart analyst Peter Brandt issued a fresh warning that the second-largest cryptocurrency could collapse below $500. His bearish outlook has raised fresh concerns about ETH’s ability to withstand mounting selling pressure, particularly as market uncertainty continues to weigh on investor sentiment.

In a November 24 post on X, Peter Brandt pointed to Ethereum’s deteriorating weekly chart structure, suggesting that ETH is approaching a critical point within a multi-year consolidation pattern.

The weekly chart above indicates a large symmetrical triangle that has formed over several market cycles. Its upper boundary is defined by a descending resistance line stretching from Ethereum’s November 2021 peak near $4,800, while the lower boundary consists of an ascending support line originating around the 2022 bear-market bottom.

Together, these converging trendlines have gradually narrowed Ethereum’s trading range, setting the stage for a potentially decisive breakout or breakdown.

Sources indicate that ETH briefly broke above the triangle’s upper resistance during its 2025 rally, eventually reaching a fresh all-time high near $4,954 in August. However, the bullish breakout failed to produce a sustained upward move, with the cryptocurrency subsequently reversing direction.

The resulting decline has produced a series of lower highs and renewed selling pressure throughout 2026, bringing ETH increasingly close to the triangle’s lower boundary.

Brandt’s bearish outlook hinges on Ethereum losing its long-standing ascending support trendline, a development that could undermine a chart structure that has supported several significant recovery attempts since 2022.

Using $1,648 as the current reference price, ETH would need to shed approximately 16.1% to revisit the critical $1,383 support level. However, the classical chartist’s more alarming outlook points to a potential plunge below $500 if the cryptocurrency fails to defend this structural floor.

In a recent development, A drop from $1,648 to $500 would translate into a staggering 69.7% decline. Even if ETH first falls to $1,383, it would still face another 63.8% downside before reaching $500.

This distinction is important because the sub-$500 projection represents a much deeper bearish scenario, not an automatic consequence of losing the immediate support level.

Such a collapse would also push Ethereum below its 2022 bear-market low, potentially marking a dramatic breakdown in its longer-term price structure.

It has been revealed that for Ethereum to begin reversing its bearish momentum, buyers must first push the altcoin king back above $1,715 and sustain a recovery beyond that threshold. Reclaiming this level would signal improving demand and offer an early sign that selling pressure is easing.

According to recent reports, the next major hurdle sits around $1,840, which coincides with ETH’s November 23 rebound high. A decisive move above this resistance would help invalidate the recent pattern of lower highs and strengthen the case for a broader recovery.

Industry observers note that on the downside, a confirmed weekly close below $1,383—particularly if followed by an unsuccessful attempt to reclaim that level—would signal a potentially damaging breakdown of Ethereum’s multi-year ascending support structure. If that scenario unfolds, ETH could face renewed selling pressure toward the psychologically crucial $1,000 mark. A deeper deterioration in market conditions could then bring Brandt’s sub-$500 projection into sharper focus.

According to recent reports, however, the bearish forecast remains conditional rather than inevitable. Ethereum has yet to lose the critical $1,383 support, leaving its ability to defend this level central to determining whether Brandt’s worst-case scenario becomes a reality.

Dogecoin co-founder Billy Markus, who is known on X as Shibetoshi Nakamoto, has explained why, in his opinion, no one can predict the prices of cryptocurrencies.

Markus shared his opinion on Wednesday in a reply to an X post with a prediction that the price of Zcash (ZEC) would fall to $100.

"my opinion is that every single cryptocurrency has an arbitrary value mostly unrelated to anything except that people believe they can make more money if others buy it from them in the future and thus all future projections are pissing in the wind," the Dogecoin co-founder wrote.

Markus did not mention Zcash or any other token by name in his reply, and his post was about every single cryptocurrency on the market, including the one he created himself.

my opinion is that every single cryptocurrency has an arbitrary value mostly unrelated to anything except people believe they can make more money if others buy it from them in the future and thus all future projections are pissing in the wind.

At the time of the post, ZEC was trading at around $728, up by 41.3% over the past year, according to price data on X.

In a recent development, the latest comment from Markus comes a week after Bitwise filed an S-1 registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for a spot Zcash ETF. According to the filing, the fund is set to trade on the Texas Stock Exchange under the ticker ZEC, and it will not stake ZEC or use shielded transactions.

Markus created Dogecoin together with Jackson Palmer in December 2013. The two developers based the cryptocurrency on the Doge meme with a Shiba Inu dog, and they debuted it as a joke about the crypto market of that time.

Markus has noted in the past that it took him a couple of hours to write the code of Dogecoin. In 2021, Markus also said on X that he had sold all of his DOGE in 2015 after he lost his job, and that he got about the price of a used Honda Civic for it.

Since then, Markus has stayed active on X under the Shibetoshi Nakamoto name, and he often replies to posts about crypto prices, forecasts and upcoming tokens.

In June 2022, Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates spoke about crypto and NFTs at the TechCrunch Sessions: Climate conference.

"As an asset class, it's 100% based on the greater fool theory — that somebody's going to pay more for it than I do," Gates said.

Earlier, at the Berkshire Hathaway annual meeting in April 2022, Warren Buffett said that he would not buy all of the Bitcoin in the world even for $25.

"If you told me you own all of the bitcoin in the world and you offered it to me for $25, I wouldn't take it because what would I do with it?" Buffett mentioned.

In a recent development, according to Buffett, Bitcoin does not produce anything. At the same meeting, Buffett compared it with farmland and apartment buildings, and he noted that he would pay for a share of them because farmland produces food and apartments produce rent.

Tesla kills $41,990 Model Y AWD: all-wheel drive now costs $8,000 more

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (818 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla has pulled the $41,990 Model Y All-Wheel Drive from its US online configurator.
  • The trim lasted just over nine months.
  • Here’s what Tesla’s US Model Y design studio lists as of today (prices before the destination fee):.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla has pulled the $41,990 Model Y All-Wheel Drive from its US online configurator. The cheapest dual-motor Model Y you can order now is the Model Y Premium AWD at $49,990, an $8,000 jump.

The trim lasted just over nine months. Tesla released it in early February, and it’s gone without a word from the company.

Here’s what Tesla’s US Model Y design studio lists as of today (prices before the destination fee):.

When Tesla launched the base Model Y AWD in February, it was basically the stripped-down Model Y with a second motor. It had 294 miles of range, did 0-60 mph in 4.6 seconds and kept the same cut-down cabin as the base RWD. At a $2,000 premium over the single-motor version, it was the most sensible AWD pricing Tesla had offered in years.

And the AWD trim isn’t the only change. In February, the Premium RWD cost $44,990 and the Premium AWD cost $48,990. Both are now $1,000 higher.

Add it up and the cheapest all-wheel-drive Model Y went from $41,990 to $49,990 in nine months. That’s a 19% increase.

Industry observers note that the timing isn’t great for Tesla’s competitive position. Chevrolet’s 2027 Equinox EV LT 1 AWD starts at $40,295 before destination, with 307 miles of EPA range. Ford’s Mustang Mach-E Select AWD starts at $40,795.

Both now undercut Tesla’s cheapest AWD crossover by more than $9,000.

According to recent reports, if you live somewhere it snows and you were shopping for a upcoming Model Y, the math just got a lot worse. You can still find some base AWD units in Tesla’s inventory, but once those are gone, that’s it.

Recent findings suggest that this is also the latest cut in a year of Tesla shrinking its lineup. Elon Musk killed the Model S and Model X in January to free up Fremont for Optimus, and Cybertruck production is winding down. Meanwhile, the most recent latest Tesla is the $61,990 Model Y L, which sits at the top of the range, not the bottom.

According to recent reports, we liked this trim. It was the first time in a long time that Tesla treated all-wheel drive as a $2,000 option rather than a huge upsell bundled with a nicer interior, and it put the Model Y right in the price bracket of the Equinox EV and Mach-E with AWD.

Now it’s gone, and the Premium trims went up $1,000 on top of that. Tesla didn’t explain either move. It rarely does anymore.

Recent findings suggest that there are two plausible reasons. Either Tesla is tight on Model Y build slots and would rather fill them with higher-margin Premium trims, or the cheap AWD simply wasn’t selling. We don’t know which. But both explanations land in the same place for buyers: a more expensive Model Y.

In a recent development, tesla is not going to keep 6 different model Y trims especially when the most expensive trim in the Model YL is selling. They will definitely squeeze out as much money from selling more expensive trims so the lowest end trim will most likely be next to go.

And Tesla has a habit of this. The “Standard” name for its cheaper Model Y and Model 3 lasted a few months. The single-motor Cybertruck, the only version that made sense, was gone within days. Cheaper trims show up, get a news cycle, and quietly disappear.

Recent findings suggest that that’s a problem for a manufacturer whose consumer lineup is shrinking down to two cars. The Model Y is Tesla’s volume. Thinning it out at the bottom is the opposite of what you’d do if growing EV sales were the priority.

How long before the $39,990 RWD goes the same way?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BitMine, the world’s largest Ethereum [ETH] DAT, has reportedly reached investments (including crypto) worth $11.1 billion as of 23rd November.

According to a recent update, the organization now holds 6,085,564 ETH, valued at approximately $10.4 billion at $1,713 per token, along with 216 Bitcoin [BTC]. This, after BitMine purchased 7,819 ETH over the past week.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, the tech giant has staked 5.22 million ETH, representing approximately 86% of its holdings. BitMine estimates that its current staked holdings could generate $245 million in annualized revenue, potentially rising to $286 million once all its ETH is staked.

At the same time, SharpLink repurchased $10 million worth of its own shares (SBET), signalling its confidence in the tech giant’s long-term strategy and its current valuation.

Industry observers note that for SharpLink, the move is also linked to its Ethereum treasury strategy. The organization aims to increase its ETH per share, which measures how much Ethereum backs each outstanding company share.

By reducing the number of shares in circulation through buybacks, SharpLink can potentially increase this metric without purchasing additional ETH.

These accumulation strategies coincided with ETH’s price trading at $1,692.78 following a drop of 1.9% at press time.

According to recent reports, despite a drop below the $2K price level, however, crypto analyst Michaël van de Poppe pointed out that Ethereum’s performance against Bitcoin has remained relatively stable. In fact, over the past two weeks, Bitcoin saw a sharp 25% decline.

That’s a sign of strength, as generally, markets would be absolutely collapsing when it comes to altcoins vs. Bitcoin.

This is noteworthy because altcoins typically suffer heavier losses than Bitcoin during market downturns as investors move towards relatively safer assets. ETH’s ability to hold its ground against BTC could therefore indicate improving relative strength and potentially growing investor interest.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Electric truck operator Nevoya is expanding its deal with Meta with the fresh deployment of 25 Class 8 battery-electric trucks on the Interstate 10 (I-10) between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona … but Meta won’t be shipping any products.

The second major trucking deal between Facebook parent company Meta and electric truck operator Nevoya will put 25 newly introduced battery-electric semis on I-10, running freight between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona. But Meta isn’t buying trucks, hiring drivers or shipping its own products. Instead, Zuck’s company helping pay for someone else’s cleaner freight through environmental attribute certificates (EACs), a carbon credit mechanism that lets companies claim the emissions benefits of electric trucking without operating the trucks themselves.

“Coming back to Nevoya for a second corridor reflects what we look for in our value chain work: partners that can scale, and agreements we can repeat, stated Devon Lake, Head of Net Zero Strategy, Meta. “Freight is part of the emissions footprint of building and operating our data centers, and multi-year commitments like this help address our scope 3 emissions and make electric trucking available and competitive on the routes that serve the regions where we build.”.

Industry observers note that meta was one of several buyers in the DC-based Center for Green Market Activation (GMA) buyers’ alliance. The group’s collective EAC purchases supported Nevoya’s initial 63-truck deployment on the Houston–Dallas corridor back in May. This new Agreement, however, is a standalone deal between Nevoya and Meta only, and gives Meta an established framework to open more electric truck corridors in the future.

This clever application of these agreements is what makes the Dallas-Houston run stand out, with GMA calling it, “the first large-scale application of book and claim to zero-emission trucking.” The tech giant adds that this arrangement helps client companies overcome existing barriers to EV adoption while enabling Nevoya to deploy fresh trucks, “where they deliver the strongest commercial and operational value.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin's long-term trend value, based on various models like "Plan B", has been set ridiculously high, so chasing targets set by those models might not be the best decision out there, considering modern market conditions.
  • A revised Bitcoin Power Law model sets BTC's long-term price at $99,000, which is almost $50,000 below the $146,725 estimate that has been used by the traditional Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) model.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. Bitcoin's long-term trend value, based on various models like "Plan B", has been set ridiculously high, so chasing targets set by those models might not be the best decision out there, considering modern market conditions.

A revised Bitcoin Power Law model sets BTC's long-term price at $99,000, which is almost $50,000 below the $146,725 estimate that has been used by the traditional Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) model.

The creator of the newer, accordingly more accurate model believes the Bitcoin Power Law is still valid, but the fair value is certainly nowhere near the relevant market conditions.

One way or another, the newer models still set the current price threshold at one of the lowest historical levels in the history of the asset—approximately the 1st percentile of its distribution, which means that it stands among 60 of Bitcoin's daily closes that fell below this threshold.

The new model uses a completely different method for calculation: Quantile Regression instead of Ordinary Least Squares (OLS). The main difference is that OLS guesses Bitcoin's price trend based on its historical averages, while QR uses specific points in the price distribution, not an average. Essentially, the newer calculation model smoothens out extremes that made OLS less accurate.

Despite the newer calculation and estimation approach, the improved calculation algorithm and everything else, models are estimating, not making solid predictions.

There are thousands of other factors to consider when determining Bitcoin's next move, so any kind of model is useful only for evaluating the momentum and historical significance of the most recent movements.

The model also places its 0.1 percentile at $55,185, a level below which Bitcoin has closed only six times. The creator argues that only the lower part of Bitcoin's price distribution, between the 0.1 and 5th percentiles, may continue following the Power Law, while higher levels gradually move down towards this lower boundary.

The model also uses Protocol Time instead of Calendar Time. Still, its creator maintains that the Power Law is not broken. The problem, according to this view, is how previous models measured it and how much they allowed market bubbles to influence the results.

Here are the coolest e-motorcycles and gear we saw at EICMA 2026

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every year, the world’s largest motorcycle companies (and plenty of the world’s smallest motorcycle companies, too) converge on Milan, Italy for Europe’s premier motorcycle showcase.
  • Below is a list of the best things I saw while walking around the show this year, presented in no particular order.
  • LiveWire came to EICMA with perhaps its most diverse electric two-wheeler lineup yet, showing just how far the manufacturer has expanded beyond the premium electric motorcycles that originally defined the Harley-Davidson spin-off.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every year, the world’s largest motorcycle companies (and plenty of the world’s smallest motorcycle companies, too) converge on Milan, Italy for Europe’s premier motorcycle showcase. That means that all of the newest electric motorcycle announcements happen in one place, and we get a chance to check out the coolest developments and most interesting latest gear.

Below is a list of the best things I saw while walking around the show this year, presented in no particular order.

LiveWire came to EICMA with perhaps its most diverse electric two-wheeler lineup yet, showing just how far the manufacturer has expanded beyond the premium electric motorcycles that originally defined the Harley-Davidson spin-off.

According to recent reports, the latest S4 Honcho family was a major focus, including the street-oriented Honcho Street, off-road Honcho Trail, and newly unveiled Honcho Skate, a stripped-down addition to the modular platform. The booth also included LiveWire’s larger S2 electric motorcycles, creating a pretty broad spectrum from lightweight urban machines up through full-size highway-capable electric motorcycles.

It has been revealed that the other massive piece of the booth was DUST Moto, which LiveWire acquired earlier this year. The production-intent DUST Hightail was displayed alongside the newly revealed DUST Spur, giving LiveWire an immediate presence in the increasingly popular lightweight electric dirt bike category.

Add in STACYC’s electric balance bikes for young riders, and the entire booth almost looked like an electric two-wheeler progression chart: start a kid on a STACYC, move up through lightweight DUST and Honcho machines, and eventually graduate to a full-size LiveWire.

GR1T Motorcycles is a relatively young European electric motorcycle startup that caught my eye at EICMA with its G1 platform, a lightweight electric motorcycle designed and engineered in Italy. The basic recipe is pretty compelling: 130 km/h (81 mph) top speed, 11 kW of continuous power and 26.6 kW (36 hp) peak, all while weighing just 130 kg (287 lb).

It has been revealed that perhaps most importantly for urban riders, its roughly 6 kWh battery is actually split into two removable 3 kWh packs, meaning apartment dwellers can pull the batteries out and charge them inside. They’re big, but removing them is doable.

GR1T’s bikes therefore pack in around 50% more battery capacity than most electric motorcycles in this size and weight class, meaning roughly 50% more range, as well.

There are also some interesting and clever design choices, like the underslung rear suspension and the triple-camera system that includes front and rear dashcams plus a cockpit-facing camera for recording the rider.

Industry observers note that the clever part of the overall design scheme is that GR1T isn’t developing a separate platform for every motorcycle. The same basic G1 chassis, motor, batteries, belt drive, and electronics underpin four versions: the G1S Street, G1X Scrambler, G1XR Raider, and utility-oriented G1M Mission.

Prices are set to start at €8,495 including VAT, putting these squarely in that emerging category of reasonably affordable, lightweight electric motorcycles that have enough speed for real-world commuting without chasing superbike performance.

According to recent reports, there’s an vital caveat, though: these aren’t production motorcycles yet. GR1T claims it is presently fundraising, with factory development and pre-orders set to follow after funding closes and first deliveries now targeted for the first half of 2028.

So the bikes aren’t quite ready for primetime yet, but it’s definitely a company to watch.

Real Motors brought one of the more visually striking electric motorcycles to EICMA with Project: ARES, a futuristic electric café racer that the American startup describes as an “Electric Analog” machine – basically an attempt to preserve the raw, mechanical connection of motorcycling while ditching unnecessary screens and gadgetry.

And there’s plenty of performance underneath the sci-fi bodywork: Real Motors lists a 75 kW (100 hp) motor, a 15 kWh battery, a 120 mph (192 km/h) top speed, and an estimated weight of 485 lb (220 kg).

The analog analogy is spot on, with the display probably the simplest and most straightforward I’ve ever seen on an electric motorcycle. There’s also no app, no subscription, and no digital handcuffs. The bike is very much the electric equivalent of a simple ICE bike that just rides, albeit with a much nicer ride.

Unlike many of the futuristic concepts scattered around EICMA, ARES is actually headed toward limited production.

Sources indicate that real Motors prepares to build just 250 examples in its first LOT 01 production run, with pricing starting at $20,000 and North American deliveries targeted for early 2027. European deliveries are expected after homologation is completed.

The manufacturer has also brought former LiveWire CTO Vance Strader onto the project as it makes the difficult transition from a very cool prototype into an actual production motorcycle.

Sources indicate that I actually had the chance to do a spin on the bike, and so I’ll be reporting back on the experience. But you can tell from my smile below that the ride was quite an experience!

Seatylock has been my go-to e-bike lock manufacturer for several years now, and I use their locks for my several e-bikes and my wife’s e-bike too.

Industry observers note that now Seatylock has returned with some even more impressive locks. The company demonstrated off its fresh Ultra D28 lock, which is both angle grinder-proof and wide enough to lock the wheel of a motorcycle. It solves the problem of how do you make a lock strong enough for a motorcycle but also small and light enough that you can actually carry it with you, unlike a massive chain lock that usually stays where you park your motorcycle overnight.

In the image below, you can see the shackle next to an exposed section demonstrating the diamond coating that essentially destroys angle grinder discs – even diamond coated discs.

The company also has a slightly smaller version of the same lock designed for bicycles.

Sources indicate that both will absolutely destroy even the toughest angle grinder discs. Sure, eventually someone could cut through them, but it may take a dozen discs and by that point the thief has moved on to an easier target.

At EICMA 2026, Royal Enfield continued expanding its electric motorcycle ambitions with its Flying Flea sub-brand, showcasing the scrambler-style motorcycle alongside its growing lineup of lightweight, retro-inspired electric motorcycles.

There were several interesting colorways and customized designs on display, showcasing the Flying Flea’s stylish design.

The newly introduced models blend Royal Enfield’s classic design heritage with modern electric technology, targeting urban riders and those looking for a fun, approachable electric motorcycle rather than a high-performance machine.

With distinctive styling, compact proportions, and an emphasis on accessible riding, the Flying Flea lineup represents Royal Enfield’s effort to carve out a place in the emerging market for smaller electric motorcycles while maintaining the character that has made its gasoline-powered bikes so popular.

Yamaha revealed off its newly introduced NMAX E electric scooter, bringing battery-powered performance to one of the brand’s most recognizable urban scooter families.

Designed as an electric alternative to the popular gasoline-powered NMAX, the new model combines familiar sporty styling with a quiet, low-maintenance electric drivetrain aimed at everyday city commuting.

The NMAX E uses Yamaha’s new compact eAxle powertrain, shared with the larger-wheeled XENTER E, and delivers up to 7.5 kW (10 hp) of peak power, putting it in the 125cc-equivalent class.

With its practical step-through design, automatic operation, and approachable performance, the NMAX E represents another step in Yamaha’s push to electrify its urban mobility lineup, particularly in European markets where scooters are already a popular alternative to cars.

Segway highlighted off a upcoming vision for safer electric scooters, including its futuristic X Cruiser concept that takes rider protection to a whole new level.

Rather than relying solely on traditional motorcycle safety equipment, the X Cruiser explores automotive-inspired features such as integrated seats with seatbelts, partial enclosures, and even a fully roofed version designed to offer additional protection from the elements.

The concept includes several configurations, ranging from a more conventional open scooter to a partially enclosed design and a fully covered model that looks like a cross between a motorcycle and a tiny electric car. While these designs are still concepts rather than production-ready scooters, they demonstrate how Segway is rethinking two-wheeled transportation by exploring ways to make electric scooters safer, more comfortable, and potentially more appealing to riders who might otherwise be hesitant to trade four wheels for two.

Eli Electric Vehicles took to EICMA 2026 to display its compact Eli Zero electric quadricycle, a tiny two-seat urban EV designed to offer much of the convenience of a car without the size, weight, or expense of a conventional automobile.

With its enclosed cabin, side-by-side seating, and ultra-compact footprint, the Eli Zero offers a practical alternative to larger vehicles for short city trips, combining the weather protection and comfort of a car with the maneuverability and efficiency of a much smaller vehicle.

It has been revealed that the firm revealed a more powerful L7e-class version of the Eli Zero that it had previously teased, expanding the vehicle’s capabilities beyond its existing L6e configuration. The new Race Edition also pushes the envelope farther with custom interior and a few extra accents to the body.

With growing interest in smaller, more efficient urban transportation, Eli’s presence at EICMA definitely underlined how the show is increasingly embracing electric mobility solutions that go beyond traditional motorcycles and scooters.

Industry observers note that NIU highlighted off its latest lineup of electric scooters, continuing the brand’s push to make battery-powered two-wheelers a practical alternative to gasoline-powered urban transportation. Known for its sleek designs, connected technology, and approachable electric scooters, NIU highlighted models aimed at a range of riders, from everyday city commuters to those looking for more powerful machines capable of keeping up with faster urban traffic.

The company highlighted off several upcoming models for the 2027 model year, with scooters that combine modern styling with features such as smartphone connectivity, smart security systems, and efficient electric drivetrains, all while maintaining the simplicity and low operating costs that make electric scooters so appealing.

While I didn’t see anything groundbreaking at the brand’s booth this year, the incremental updates look to push upcoming tech features further throughout the brand’s many models, helping more of NIU’s offerings enter that premium level that the organization has been known for.

For something a bit wilder, Honda shared its futuristic EV Outlier Concept, an electric motorcycle that explores what two-wheeled design could look like when engineers are freed from the constraints of traditional gasoline-powered motorcycles.

With its long, low-slung profile, radically different riding position, and futuristic bodywork, the EV Outlier looks more like something out of a science fiction movie than a conventional motorcycle. The concept features electric motors integrated into both wheels, giving it two-wheel drive while opening up upcoming possibilities for packaging and weight distribution.

Rather than simply replacing a combustion engine with a battery and motor, Honda used the EV Outlier to rethink the entire motorcycle layout, demonstrating how electrification could lead to entirely upcoming types of riding experiences.

While the bike remains a design concept with no announced production aims, it offers an intriguing glimpse into Honda’s vision for the future of electric motorcycles.

Vespa indicated off its next-generation electric scooter lineup at EICMA, including electric versions of the Primavera, Sprint S, and Primavera Tech. While they don’t look radically different, there’s a lot more happening underneath the familiar steel bodywork.

A new Italian-made, rare-earth-free electric motor improves efficiency and performance, while the 45 km/h Primavera and Sprint S now feature removable batteries.

The faster 67 km/h Primavera Tech gets up to 90 km of WMTC range – a 12.5% improvement – along with an updated vehicle management system and more efficient charger.
