💡 Key Takeaways
  • The South Korean FSC’s new draft bill could change things for the country’s crypto space.
  • Under the new blueprint, banks put together can own more than half of any won stablecoin issuer.
  • According to recent reports, issuers must have FSC approval and at least 5 billion won in equity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The South Korean FSC’s new draft bill could change things for the country’s crypto space. What’s what’s going on exactly?

Under the new blueprint, banks put together can own more than half of any won stablecoin issuer. A fintech company can still be the largest shareholder, but they can’t run the show alone anymore.

According to recent reports, issuers must have FSC approval and at least 5 billion won in equity. Reserves must cover 100% of tokens in circulation, and holders must be able to cash out at face value right away.

As far as exchanges go, one shareholder can hold 20% or 34% with FSC approval. They’ll also need separate licences for dealing, brokerage, and custody.

But… domestic ICOs would be legal again.

In a recent development, south Korea’s plan is a 22% tax on crypto gains above 2.5 million won a year. It was meant to kick in this January, but it looks like that date’s been pushed back to 2029.

One reason is that it’s the earliest Korea can start swapping crypto tax data with the United States.

In a recent development, if that happens, it won’t be the first delay. The tax was first proposed back in 2020 and has been shelved several times since.

Enforcement is still active though. AMBCrypto previously reported that 27 unlicensed exchange websites were blocked recently, including KuCoin, MEXC and BingX. This was after their apps were already restricted.

Users on those platforms are being nudged towards the country’s 28 licensed exchanges.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • VanEck is ending its relationship with Gemini across three spot crypto ETFs, leaving Coinbase Custody as its remaining named custodian.
  • Recent findings suggest that the asset manager disclosed in Nov.
  • It has been revealed that the agreements are scheduled to expire in February 2027, and Gemini will continue to provide services until the termination takes effect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

VanEck is ending its relationship with Gemini across three spot crypto ETFs, leaving Coinbase Custody as its remaining named custodian.

Recent findings suggest that the asset manager disclosed in Nov. 19 regulatory filings that it had notified Gemini of plans to terminate its custody and clearing agreements for its Bitcoin ETF (HODL), Ethereum ETF (ETHV) and Solana ETF (VSOL).

It has been revealed that the agreements are scheduled to expire in February 2027, and Gemini will continue to provide services until the termination takes effect. The decision also ends a separate arrangement under which Gemini facilitates Solana staking for VSOL.

The filings did not disclose the reasons for the termination or how much cryptocurrency VanEck currently holds with Gemini.

The three funds have attracted approximately $1.15 billion in cumulative net inflows since their respective releases and collectively managed $934.2 million in net assets as of Nov. 24, according to SoSoValue data.

Recent findings suggest that vanEck's Bitcoin ETF accounted for the bulk of that exposure, with $977.1 million in cumulative net inflows and $848.2 million in net assets. Its Ethereum and Solana funds recorded cumulative net inflows of $151.6 million and $19.2 million, respectively.

VanEck's decision extends beyond asset safekeeping. Gemini also provides clearing infrastructure that helps the funds settle cryptocurrency transactions associated with ETF share creations and redemptions.

Under the existing arrangements, VanEck's funds can use Gemini Clearing to complete trades negotiated with liquidity providers that are also Gemini customers.

The service has supported cash-based orders, which require the funds to purchase or sell cryptocurrencies, and in-kind transactions involving the direct transfer of digital assets.

The scheduled February 2027 exit affects two services across VanEck’s HODL, ETHV and VSOL.

Coinbase Custody stays with all three funds. The filings name no successor to Gemini’s trade clearing service.

It has been revealed that the lines track service appointments. The filings give no amount or timing for any transfers between custodians.

The connections trace each service described in the three November 19 termination filings across its scheduled effective date.

Industry observers note that the lines track service appointments. The filings give no amount or timing for any transfers between custodians.

Coinbase will continue serving the Bitcoin and Ethereum funds under their existing prime broker agreements, while the Solana fund also maintains a separate custody agreement with the organization.

VanEck did not identify a successor to Gemini's clearing services or provide a timetable for any cryptocurrency transfers between the custodians.

VanEck's decision contrasts with arrangements at other major US crypto ETF issuers that have established relationships with multiple digital asset custodians.

It has been revealed that blackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) uses Coinbase Custody as its custodian and has appointed Anchorage Digital Bank as an additional provider. Its latest quarterly report noted the fund had no immediate plans to transfer Bitcoin to Anchorage.

It has been revealed that blackRock also maintains flexibility in its trading arrangements. The fund can execute Bitcoin transactions directly with third-party counterparties or through Coinbase Prime when processing cash-based creation and redemption orders.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund maintains its primary custody and trade execution relationship with Fidelity Digital Assets, an affiliate of its sponsor. Fidelity has also appointed BitGo Bank & Trust as an additional custodian, although it reported no immediate plans to transfer Bitcoin to the company.

These arrangements allow BlackRock and Fidelity to retain additional custody providers without necessarily distributing their existing Bitcoin holdings across them.

VanEck's termination of Gemini's agreements moves in the opposite direction across three separate crypto investment products, increasing the importance of its remaining relationship with Coinbase.

Its September quarterly reports describe transactions conducted directly with liquidity providers, while earlier prospectuses also allowed alternative execution arrangements for certain trades if settlement failed.

Those existing arrangements could accommodate transactions previously handled through Gemini Clearing without VanEck appointing another dedicated clearing provider.

With the termination scheduled for February, VanEck's subsequent regulatory disclosures could reveal whether it intends to consolidate more of its trading infrastructure with Coinbase or establish latest arrangements with other institutional service providers.

Hyundai is skipping the typical mid-cycle refresh and prepares to launch a completely redesigned Kona, with a sleek upcoming style and an updated high-tech interior.

It’s been nearly four years since Hyundai introduced the second-generation Kona, meaning, like most of its models, the compact SUV was expected to receive a mid-cycle refresh.

Recent findings suggest that hyundai is apparently going straight to the third-generation model instead. Earlier this year, early-stage prototypes were spotted in Korea that looked much boxier and more rugged than the current Kona.

Since then, several test mules have been captured testing in the US, Europe, and other regions, confirming the Kona will adopt a more upright, traditional SUV design similar to the newly introduced Santa Fe, Palisade, and Tucson.

The wider, more powerful design appears to draw inspiration from Hyundai’s off-road Crater Concept, revealed at the LA Auto Show last year.

In a recent development, hyundai remarked the off-road SUV Concept was a preview of the “next evolution” of its Extreme Rugged Terrain (XRT) vehicles, such as the IONIQ 5 XRT and Palisade XRT Pro. Is the Kona next in line to receive the XRT treatment?

A post shared by SHORTS CAR (@shorts_car).

Apparent leaked images from a few months ago revealed a design that looked like a mashup of the Crater Concept and IONIQ 5, with pixelated lighting and a clamshell hood.

Sources indicate that most recently, the third-gen Hyundai Kona, codenamed “SX3,” was spotted disguised in a parking garage in Korea. The images were sent to ShortsCar, revealing the fresh Kona’s wheel design.

It has been revealed that while earlier reports suggested Hyundai planned to drop the all-electric Kona variant and would only offer gas and hybrid versions, the prototype captured in Korea is expected to be the EV model. However, Hyundai has yet to confirm powertrain or battery specs.

Sources indicate that the updates are even more evident on the inside. Previous spy images appeared to show the third-gen Hyundai Kona running Hyundai’s new Pleos Connect infotainment system, like the IONIQ 3.

In the IONIQ 3, Hyundai offers a 12.9″ or 14.6″ center infotainment screen, plus an optional driver display.

Like the current model, the third-gen Kona is expected to be available with fully electric (EV), hybrid, and gas-powered powertrains.

While Hyundai skipped the 2026 Kona EV, the electric version could return in 2027 or 2028 when the third-generation model is expected to arrive.

The hybrid version will likely use the same 1.6L hybrid engine as the upcoming Seltos, while the EV variant could offer similar powertrain and battery options to the IONIQ 3.

The IONIQ 3 is available with two battery packs in Europe and the UK: 42 kWh and 61 kWh, offering WLTP ranges of up to 213 miles (344 km) and 308 miles (497 km), respectively.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ripple has once again landed a major partnership in Türkiye, but this time around with one of the country’s largest private banks, putting XRP in the spotlight.

While this comes as part of Ripple’s growing expansion into the traditional financial space, the blockchain firm declared it has partnered with Yapı Kredi, a major Turkish private bank, to support its cryptocurrency business.

As part of the partnership agreement, Ripple Custody will help the bank to securely manage its digital assets and provide custody services for its crypto trading platform dubbed Yapı Kredi Kripto.

While the partnership demands the full integration of the Ripple custodial infrastructure, the firm revealed that Ripple Custody will be installed on the bank's own premises.

This way, Yapı Kredi will have access to adequate security and control it needs to manage all digital assets on behalf of its customers, boosting its security.

The development is significant for the bank and the broader Turkish crypto market; it also marks a major milestone for Ripple as the firm claims to be the only custody service provider presently supporting leading Turkish banks licensed by the CMB as crypto asset custodians.

It is important to note that Türkiye currently stands as one of the world's top 10 retail crypto markets, with XRP recorded as one of its most widely used cryptocurrencies.

With Yapı Kredi now fortifying its position as a major player in Türkiye’s fast-growing crypto market, its partnership with the blockchain firm associated with XRP is likely to open newly introduced opportunities for XRP while positioning it for bigger adoption in the country.

  • It has been revealed that in a recent community note, Ethereum Foundation researcher Kev Wedderburn noted aims have been in the works for years to mitigate quantum risks, but recent AI changes will prompt changes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Ethereum Foundation is planning a security upgrade to protect the network against artificial intelligence (AI) and quantum computing risks. This year, the wider sector has faced hacks that drained billions from the market, prompting devs to roll out security updates.

It has been revealed that in a recent community note, Ethereum Foundation researcher Kev Wedderburn noted aims have been in the works for years to mitigate quantum risks, but recent AI changes will prompt changes. It has doubled its security protocol team to beef up defenses on multiple fronts.

In a recent development, A major problem is the limited timeframe and amount of work required for a comprehensive upgrade. The Foundation projects it will be harder than Merge, though it has more advanced tools at its disposal. Ethereum Merge saw the network move to a Proof-of-Stake consensus mechanism following heated debates over energy consumption.

According to recent reports, now security questions are resonating in crypto spaces, with developers rolling out roadmaps ahead of 2027. Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin stressed AI security risks, privacy threats, and manipulation concerns while explaining the network’s roadmap.

The network build covers three areas: consensus, owners, and data. First, validators sign with hash-based keys, while wallets let users seamlessly pivot to hash-based signatures.

Recent findings suggest that “Moving fast makes it easier to ship bugs, so formal verification and security work will have to keep up with the pace of protocol development; cutting corners here would defeat the whole purpose of the upgrade. In response to this, the EF has doubled the size of its protocol security team.”.

Industry observers note that according to the note, every layer will adapt, even if it means delaying current features. This includes tools being built, as they will be monitored for overall network safety.

Recently, Justin Drake, an Ethereum researcher, tipped their team to complete a post-quantum upgrade by 2028. Quantum fears are dominating blockchain security conversations because supercomputers are developing so swiftly.

Industry observers note that if these computers break the cryptography, bad actors could drain billions in Bitcoin and other assets. While Ethereum has made significant progress to prevent Q-Day attacks, Bitcoin is largely behind due to governance setbacks.

The largest crypto by market cap plunged below $60,000 amid crushing low sentiment from whales. Ethereum is down 2.4%, trading at $1,657 after a negative few months.
